ARVO metadata separately reports `c8da8302dbd59406d7d7975845fc842b951aacbc` / `dee5006b3da38604b1a7e49e80b747f2443653ba`, and the staged `patch.diff` is commit `58a2fdb5b1ad1efafef455d66a9cbfb93c3fae9d` (`Fuzz: Remove unsupported assert calls`), but neither touches the reviewed cleanup path. Local history in the staged checkout contains commit `d31ae132ad6c9d8785f41d4c118484deac38dbcd` (`Stack: Avoid double free/heap use after free`), which explicitly fixes OSS-Fuzz issue 14567 by nulling `userTokenPolicies` and zeroing `userTokenPoliciesSize` after the first free.

classification.classification_note: The observed memory error is a stale-pointer reuse during a second cleanup of `UA_AccessControl`: the first cleanup frees `userTokenPolicies`, leaves the pointer and size live, and the second cleanup re-enters array clearing and reads a `UA_String` field from the freed array.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is only four bytes: `20 19 03 00`. In `fuzz_binary_message`, those bytes are consumed entirely by `UA_memoryManager_setLimitFromLast4Bytes`, so no OPC UA message bytes remain after `size -= 4`; the only attacker-controlled state is the custom allocator limit `0x00031920 = 203040`. Under that low-memory condition, `setDefaultConfig()` still succeeds far enough to allocate `accessControl.userTokenPolicies` as a two-element `UA_UserTokenPolicy` array. A later allocation inside `addDefaultNetworkLayers()` then fails, and `UA_ServerConfig_setMinimalCustomBuffer()` takes its error branch and calls `UA_ServerConfig_clean(config)`. During this first cleanup, `deleteMembers_default()` frees `ac->userTokenPolicies` but does not clear `ac->userTokenPolicies` or `ac->userTokenPoliciesSize`. The fuzzer then sees `UA_ServerConfig_setDefault()` fail and calls `UA_Server_delete(server)`, which invokes `UA_ServerConfig_clean(&server->config)` a second time on the same embedded config. That second cleanup re-enters `deleteMembers_default()` with the dangling `userTokenPolicies` pointer and stale size `2`, so `UA_Array_delete()` walks the already freed 144-byte array and `String_clear()` reads a `UA_String` member from freed memory. The saved ASan trace reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/ua_types.c:140`. The staged `patch.diff` and reported `fix_commit` are unrelated to this path; the matching local fix is `d31ae13`, which nulls `userTokenPolicies` and zeros `userTokenPoliciesSize` immediately after the first free.

source.description: First project-code materialization of attacker-controlled state on the crashing path: the last four bytes of the witness become the global allocator limit used by all later `UA_malloc`/`UA_calloc` checks.
source.value_from: The exact staged PoC is the 4-byte file `20 19 03 00`, interpreted little-endian as `0x00031920 = 203040`. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, `size -= 4` then leaves zero message bytes, so this allocator limit is the only attacker-controlled value that reaches the vulnerability path.

sink.description: ASan crash site. During the second cleanup, `String_clear` reads the `data` field from a `UA_String` embedded in the already freed `UA_UserTokenPolicy` array, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free READ 8.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 8` at `String_clear /src/open62541/src/ua_types.c:140:24`, 8 bytes inside the 144-byte region that was freed earlier by `deleteMembers_default`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The first error cleanup frees `userTokenPolicies` but leaves both the pointer and the nonzero element count live in `ac`, so later cleanup reuses a dangling array base.
root_cause.note: Local fix commit `d31ae13` matches this exact obligation by adding `ac->userTokenPolicies = NULL; ac->userTokenPoliciesSize = 0;` immediately after the `UA_Array_delete` call.

tainted_value_origin.description: The witness's last four bytes are interpreted as a little-endian uint32 and stored into the fuzz-only global allocator limit.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged input bytes `20 19 03 00` decode to `memoryLimit = 203040`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness has `size == 4`, so this guard succeeds, the custom allocator limit is taken from the input trailer, and execution continues into `UA_ServerConfig_setDefault()` with zero remaining message bytes.

first_cleanup.description: The saved free stack names this exact call as the first free site, proving the low-memory path fails inside `addDefaultNetworkLayers()` and performs an initial config cleanup before returning error.

second_cleanup.description: After config setup fails, the fuzzer deletes the server. That teardown performs a second cleanup on the same embedded `server->config` object.

coarse_trace.summary: The 4-byte witness is consumed entirely as the custom allocator-limit trailer, so `memoryLimit` becomes 203040 and no OPC UA message bytes remain.

Default config setup allocates a two-element `accessControl.userTokenPolicies` array, then a later low-memory failure in `addDefaultNetworkLayers()` sends `UA_ServerConfig_setMinimalCustomBuffer()` into its error-cleanup path.
The first cleanup frees `userTokenPolicies` but leaves the pointer and size live in `UA_AccessControl`, creating stale config state.

The harness deletes the server after config failure, so a second cleanup re-enters `deleteMembers_default()` on the stale access-control state and `String_clear()` reads from the already freed `userTokenPolicies` array.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact staged PoC is the 4-byte blob `20 19 03 00`; this call interprets those bytes as little-endian `0x00031920 = 203040` and stores that value in the global `memoryLimit`. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, `size -= 4` then leaves zero message bytes, so this allocator limit is the only attacker-controlled state on the crashing path.

With `allowAnonymous = true` and the built-in `usernamePasswordsSize = 2` table enabled, this computes `policies = 2`, allocates a two-element `UA_UserTokenPolicy` array, and stores both the heap pointer and the nonzero element count in `ac`. ASan's allocation stack identifies this exact call (`UA_memoryManager_calloc -> UA_AccessControl_default:266`) as the allocation site of the later-freed 144-byte region.

depends_on.via: memoryLimit controls the custom allocator used by UA_Array_new

fine_trace.note: After `setDefaultConfig()` has already populated `config->accessControl`, a later allocation inside `addDefaultNetworkLayers()` fails under the same low-memory limit. The saved free stack proves this exact error branch executes first by naming `UA_ServerConfig_setMinimalCustomBuffer:261` as the context that calls `UA_ServerConfig_clean(config)`.

Root cause. During that first cleanup, `deleteMembers_default` frees the 144-byte `userTokenPolicies` array from step 2 but does not clear `ac->userTokenPolicies` or `ac->userTokenPoliciesSize`. The embedded config therefore retains a dangling array base together with stale `size = 2` for any later cleanup pass.

Because `UA_ServerConfig_setDefault()` returned the same non-GOOD `retval` from step 3, the harness takes its error path and deletes the server instead of reaching any message-buffer allocation or binary-message parsing.

This second cleanup dispatch re-enters `deleteMembers_default` on the same embedded `accessControl` struct during `UA_Server_delete()`. Since step 4 left `userTokenPolicies` and `userTokenPoliciesSize` unchanged, the callback receives the dangling array pointer and stale element count `2` a second time.

Sink. In the second `deleteMembers_default -> UA_Array_delete -> UA_clear -> clearStructure` walk over the stale `UA_UserTokenPolicy` array, `String_clear` is invoked on a `UA_String` member loaded from the already freed array element. Reading `s->data` from that freed struct triggers the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/ua_types.c:140:24`.

depends_on.via: second cleanup reuses the stale array pointer and size

poc.trigger: Feed the exact 4-byte file `20 19 03 00` to `fuzz_binary_message`. The harness interprets all four bytes as the little-endian allocator-limit trailer `203040`, then subtracts 4 so no message bytes remain. Under that low-memory setup, `UA_ServerConfig_setDefault()` performs one cleanup on config-setup failure and the harness immediately performs the second cleanup via `UA_Server_delete(server)`, reproducing the ASan heap-use-after-free READ 8 in `String_clear`.
